changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6286-explain-batch-cap-from-spec.md`

- names `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` → `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` — edited by this change

  > **No value changes and no behaviour changes.** The spec exports `200`, which is what the local copy said, verified by resolving the installed package and reading the export — both statically (`dist/security/index.d.mts`) and at runtime through the same specifier the source now uses. What changes is reference identity: if the server relaxes or tightens the cap and the spec follows, the client follows too, instead of paginating at the old boundary with no signal anywhere. The cap's whole point is that an over-cap request is refused with `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` rather than truncated, so a client that silently disagrees with it is exactly the drift `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` argues about — and could not catch here, because both of its scanners skip non-exported declarations and this const was module-local (objectui#5899).

### `.changeset/8841-tree-view-config-derive.md`

- names `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` → `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` — edited by this change

  > **What was wrong.** `@object-ui/types` published `TreeViewConfig` as a hand-written interface — a copy of the protocol's `ListView.tree` block under a second name — and the copy declared a fifth key, `titleField`. `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` refuses that key there by name: `TreeConfigSchema` is a `strictObject` since spec #15469 closed the `.passthrough()` window 17.3.0 left open. So this package's published face accepted what the contract rejects, and an author who followed `@object-ui/types` was refused at publish with `Unrecognized key(s) on this tree configuration: 'titleField'`. The copy was invisible to `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs`, which matches spec symbols BY NAME — a hand copy renamed away from the spec's symbol has nothing for its rule 1 to match (objectui#4592's recorded blind spot).

### `.changeset/console-form-container-specs-one-declaration-5596.md`

- names `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` → `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` — edited by this change

  > Both types are therefore **derived from the spec's own `FormSection` / `FormView` with named narrowings** — the repo's sanctioned form for a spec-shaped local type (`scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs`) — rather than restated. Every key the two layers agree on comes from the spec and cannot fall behind it; the four positions where this layer is deliberately narrower are each named in an `Omit` list and restated once next to its reason: `fields` keeps the converged 26-key leaf (deriving it would silently re-open #5542), and `label` / `description` / `visibleWhen` / `visibleOn` keep the shapes this repo's renderers and evaluators actually consume rather than the spec's `I18nLabel` and `ExpressionInput`. `apps/console`'s `submitBehavior` union — previously hand-written under the comment "Mirrors the spec FormView.submitBehavior union" — is now read back off the shared type, making the mirror structural. `@object-ui/app-shell` re-exports both names from its package root (type-only, erased at build — nothing is added to the bundle), because a type that cannot be imported is a type that gets retyped.

### `.changeset/listview-comment-pair-4559.md`

- names `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` → `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` — edited by this change

  > **objectui#4966 — `formatActionLabel`'s docblock now sits above `formatActionLabel`.** It had drifted two declarations up, so the exported `parseSortConfig` carried two stacked leading comments and the helper carried none. This one was not cosmetic: because `parseSortConfig` is exported, `vite-plugin-dts` copied the misattributed block into `dist/ListView.d.ts`, so every consumer's editor hover and TypeDoc introduced the sort parser with a sentence about action labels. Moving the block removes it from the `.d.ts`; `formatActionLabel` is module-private, so its now-correct docblock does not appear there. It also matters to `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs`, whose rule 2 reads the comment block *attached* to a declaration — a misattributed docblock is the mechanism by which a claim gets scored against the wrong symbol. This block carries no spec-alignment phrase, so nothing fired today.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `733fd5ac6` (merge-base with origin/main): 2 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1669 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2263 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36396304972)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `22226a8e9bde1f06f47c2faaa698cfb9148793de`

Isolated adversarial contract review of PR #10934 (card objectui#10916). Inputs: the card and its five comments (the dev's `os-dev-report` `5866360163` read as a claim), objectui#9860 (ruling C) with all 17 comments, the gate workflow and `scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs` on `origin/main`, precedents objectui#10080 / PR #10089, objectui#3177 and objectui#3162, objectstack#20369 and objectstack `origin/main` `2c310705f` (`packages/spec/src/ui/report.zod.ts`, `joined-report-block-type.test.ts`, `i18n.zod.ts`, `identifiers.zod.ts`, `strict-object.ts`), the PR body, diff, file list and the 43 check-runs on the head, and the objectui tree at the head and at `origin/main` `733fd5ac6`. Every reading below is this seat's own unless marked as the dev's claim. Generic parameters are written as UPPERCASE WORDS.

### ① Derived judgments

**Not a weakening of the gate.** The gate (ruling C) is objectui compiling against spec `main`; the old line was a consumer-side tripwire, `true satisfies IsUnknown OF SpecJoinedReportBlock`, whose docblock said its own failure is the instruction to re-run the triage and burn down. The typed schema landed upstream (objectstack#20369, merge `681868ca7c`, an ancestor of objectstack `main`), the tripwire fired as designed, and the burn-down cannot land yet: on the installed 17.4.0 the derived type would be `unknown` (read from the installed `dist/page.zod-DiFhqKNm.d.ts`: `declare const JoinedReportBlockSchema: z.ZodTypeAny` and `type JoinedReportBlock = z.input OF typeof JoinedReportBlockSchema`, with zod 4.4.3 resolving from the spec's own directory). The claim comment `5865635869` fenced exactly this: a burn-down that changes the published declaration stops and becomes a second slice. What the old pin caught — the spec typing the block — is now a recorded fact rather than a pending event; `any` is still refused (the `IsAny` pin is unchanged and the state pin refuses `any`). Nothing is skipped, disabled or ts-ignored, no workflow moved, and the gate is green on the head because the file compiles, not because it was excluded.

**The dual admission is justified and load-bearing.** Read at the head: `erased` is what the installed 17.4.0 declares (the pull-request `Type Check` compiles this file against it); `typed` is what spec `main` declares (the gate compiles the same file against it). One file, two compilers, so one pin admitting both is the only shape that compiles on both without a skip. Verified in a worktree at the head with a frozen offline install: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` in `packages/types` gives exit 0 with 0 diagnostics on the installed spec; deleting the `erased` arm gives exit 2 with exactly one diagnostic, TS1360 `Type '"erased"' does not satisfy the expected type '"typed"'` at `_specJoinedReportBlockTyping` — so the arm is load-bearing today and the dev's ablation A5 reproduces. The file was restored to blob `a1b2c707461e`, equal to HEAD.

**Declared limit, judged real and acceptable.** A re-erasure on spec `main` before the bump is type-identical to the installed 17.4.0 (both are the bare `z.ZodTypeAny`), so the state pin admits it on the gate. This seat looked for a compile-time marker caused by this schema that could refuse it: objectstack#20369 added `JoinedReportBlockParsed` to the `ui` entry, but it is a type-only export and a type's presence cannot be probed conditionally at compile time (a missing type import is a hard error on 17.4.0); the schema value's own annotation is the same predicate as the erasure and adds nothing. So the dev's falsification of Zone 2 item 3 stands. The window is covered at the producer: `packages/spec/src/ui/joined-report-block-type.test.ts` on objectstack `main` carries seven `@ts-expect-error` lines that become TS2578 under `check:test-typecheck` the moment the block is `unknown` again (objectstack#20369's own reverse leg reports 7 TS2578 and 2 TS18046 on reverting item 1).

**What forces the burn-down at the bump, and it fires.** The Spec Main Shape Gate runs `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm type-check --continue` and no test (workflow read on `origin/main`), so the forcing lives in vitest, which the required `Test` aggregator runs on every pull request including a spec-bump PR. Two rows read the INSTALLED spec's built `.d.ts` with the TypeScript checker: the typing row (must read `erased`) and the version row (must read `17.4.0`). Verified: the file gives 47 passed on the installed spec; with the version row's expectation changed to `17.3.0`, 1 failed / 46 passed with the row's own message; with the reader forced to answer `erased` for every symbol, the lit control (`ReportSort` must read `typed`) is the one row that fails, 1 failed / 46 passed — so the control is a real control and the typing row cannot pass through a dead reader. The reader resolves `@objectstack/spec/package.json` through `createRequire(import.meta.url)` from the test file's own directory, which is `packages/types/node_modules/@objectstack/spec`, the same symlink `tsc` resolves; the lockfile holds exactly one 17.4.0 entry and the worktree's virtual store one copy, so there is no hoisted duplicate to read instead. The exact `17.4.0` match is sound rather than churn: npm's `latest` is 17.4.0 (the newest of eight 17.x releases), objectstack's own retirement text in `report.zod.ts` names 17.5.0 as the next release, and #20369 is on `main` behind that release, so any bump moves the version row and the typing row together. ⚠️ What the row forces is an edit to this file; which edit (delete the `erased` arm, derive the published interface in its own `Clause-②: yes` slice) is prose in the failure message and the docblock, which is the same forcing the old pin offered. That slice will carry its own contract review, so this is recorded, not held against the PR.

**The seven probes, each read against spec main today and mutated.** Spec `main`'s `JoinedReportBlockSchema` is `lazySchema` wrapping `strictObject(options, shape)`, with `lazySchema` returning its factory's type and `strictObject` a closed `z.object(shape).strict()`; the shape declares `name` (`SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema`, a `z.string()`), `label` and `description` (`I18nLabelSchema.optional()`, a union of `z.string()` and `InlineLocaleMapSchema`, whose input is `Record OF string, string` with `key` and `defaultValue` typed `never`), `type` (enum `tabular`/`summary`/`matrix`, defaulted), `dataset`, `rows`, `columns` (`z.array(z.string())`, the matrix across-axis), `values`, `runtimeFilter`, `order`; `objectName`, `object`, `filter`, `groupings` and friends are alias-table entries aimed at `dataset` / `runtimeFilter` / `rows`, and `chart` is a `guidance` entry (objectstack#20161's retirement prescription), not a declared key. So the recorded divergences are TRUE of spec main today: `name` and `type` agree; the local `{ default, translations }` label arm is not assignable to the locale map; `columns` is dimension names there and column objects here; the five local-only keys are undeclared and the closed schema refuses them; the five spec-only keys are exactly `dataset`, `rows`, `values`, `runtimeFilter`, `order`; the spec type has no index signature. To ask whether the probes can be satisfied vacuously, this seat hand-derived the input type from that shape, pointed a verbatim copy of the PR's type machinery at it beside the REAL local interface from `spec-report.ts`, and compiled twelve variants under the package's `tsconfig.test.json`: the as-read shape gives 0 diagnostics (the triage table is consistent with the schema); spec `columns` as objects fires `_blockColumnsAreTwoConcepts` alone; spec label admitting the local object arm fires `_blockLabelObjectArmIsNotASpecLabel` alone; a new spec key fires `_specOnlyBlockKeys` alone; a branded `name` fires `_blockNameAgrees` alone; `type` gaining `joined` fires `_blockTypeAgrees` alone; `chart` declared as a `never` tombstone fires `_localOnlyBlockKeys`; `unknown` gives 0 diagnostics; `any` fires the state pin and the `IsAny` pin; `never` fires five pins. Two vacuities found: if the spec DROPS `columns`, `BlockMember` yields `never` and `[never] extends [string[]]` is true, so probe 3 stays green; if the spec drops both `label` and `description`, probe 4 stays green by the same route. Both cases fire `_localOnlyBlockKeys` (the dropped key becomes local-only), so the file as a whole is not vacuous — only the per-probe attribution is. No `boolean`-leaking conditional: every probe is tuple-wrapped and `SpecTyping` checks a non-naked type, so no probe can resolve to `boolean` and slip through `true satisfies`.
